narrativeReportMd:
# Contract R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Contract` is still the same non-abstract resource at the same canonical URL, but it has one high-impact local instance break: `Contract.term.action.reason` was remodeled from an R4 string plus sibling `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` elements into an R6 `CodeableReference`. R4 instances using any of the old reason representations need a structural transform before R6 validation, and R6 grouped reason content is not always losslessly representable in R4.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions and related local terminology artifacts. Inherited base-resource changes visible in the snapshot, including `language`, `modifierExtension`, `dom-*`, `ele-*`, and extension constraints, are excluded from local Contract findings.

## Main migration themes
The primary migration theme is representation normalization around action rationale: free text, coded reasons, and referenced justifications are consolidated into `CodeableReference`. Secondary themes are R6-to-R4 round-trip risk from a widened `author` target, low-level code generation changes from `term.text` becoming `markdown`, and business-rule review for the changed meaning of `contentDefinition.publicationDate`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Contract:TYPE_DOMAIN:Contract.term.action.reason:6f0b9a`, because it changes JSON shape and generated model shape for common action-rationale fields. No local cardinality strengthening, local modifier-flag strengthening, or required binding code removal was found.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for action reason migration policy, for deciding whether `contentDefinition.publicationDate` was used as an original publication date or a last-change date in real systems, and for interpreting example-binding terminology changes where local R6 terminology expansions were not available.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The reason remodel is probably motivated by the reusable `CodeableReference` pattern, but it could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated R4 sibling elements or adding a new optional element. The semantic date change could also have been less disruptive by adding a separate last-significant-change element.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate base-artifact reports should own inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes. Terminology and datatype reports should assess `CodeableReference`, `markdown`, participation/security role value sets, and external terminology expansions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Contract` has one clear hard local instance break: the action-reason fields are merged and retyped to `CodeableReference`. Other migration concerns are R6-only `RelatedPerson` authors, `term.text` changing to `markdown`, semantic drift in `contentDefinition.publicationDate`, and example-binding changes for action performer terminology. The main uncertainty is terminology expansion detail for external value sets not present in the local R6 package.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first transform `term.action.reason`, `reasonCode`, and `reasonReference` into the R6 `term.action.reason` array of `CodeableReference` objects. Reverse conversion should detect grouped R6 `CodeableReference` instances that contain both `concept` and `reference`, because splitting them into separate R4 arrays can lose association. Systems should also audit generated models and serializers for changed property types and target profiles, and review whether Contract publication metadata is interpreted as original publication or last significant change.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both primary StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for some terminology and semantic implications because no official diff, change rationale, narrative pages, or terminology-server expansions were available. Inherited base-resource changes were intentionally excluded rather than treated as local Contract findings.

findings.title: Contract.term.action reason fields were merged and retyped to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 represented action rationale across three sibling arrays: `reason` as string, `reasonCode` as CodeableConcept, and `reasonReference` as Reference.

semanticText.short: Why action is to be performed
semanticText.definition: Describes why the action is to be performed or not performed in textual form.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Contract.term.action.reason` was a repeating primitive string. Related but separate optional siblings carried coded reasons (`reasonCode`, example-bound to v3 PurposeOfUse) and resource references (`reasonReference`, targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Questionnaire, and QuestionnaireResponse).

newState.summary: R6 uses `Contract.term.action.reason` as a repeating CodeableReference with concept/reference content and the former reason reference targets.

binding.description: Detailed codes for the contract action reason.

semanticText.definition: Rationale for the action to be performed or not performed. Describes why the action is permitted or prohibited. Either a coded concept, or another resource whose existence justifies permitting or not permitting this action.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the separate `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` elements and makes `reason` a `CodeableReference`, allowing each array item to carry a concept, a reference, or both.

facts.note: Cardinality is unchanged, but item shape changed from primitive string to complex datatype.
The coded reason role moved into `reason.concept`.

facts.oldValue: 0..* Reference to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Questionnaire, QuestionnaireResponse
facts.note: The reference reason role moved into `reason.reference`.

facts.oldValue: Separate R4 arrays without per-item grouping between code and reference
facts.newValue: R6 CodeableReference item may group concept and reference
facts.note: R6-to-R4 conversion can lose grouping if both concept and reference are present in one item.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `reason` definition and binding combine the exact rationale wording, v3 PurposeOfUse binding, and reference target set that were split across R4 `reason`, `reasonCode`, and `reasonReference`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break. An R4 instance containing `term.action.reason` as JSON strings or using the R4 sibling properties `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` will not match the R6 element set and datatype. Conversely, an R6 `CodeableReference` object at `reason` is not a valid R4 string at the same path, and R6 items containing both `concept` and `reference` cannot be split into R4 arrays without losing their item-level association.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Action rationale can explain why a contract permits or prohibits an action. Losing or mis-associating the rationale can affect authorization, consent, or contract-administration decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the R6 `CodeableReference` pattern to represent a rationale that may be textual/coded and/or backed by a resource reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A transitional base design could have retained the R4 reason, reasonCode, and reasonReference elements while adding a new CodeableReference-based rationale element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `CodeableReference` directly models a rationale that may be coded, referenced, or both, and it removes three parallel R4 arrays that could not preserve concept/reference grouping. The break is substantial for existing R4 instances, but the less-breaking base alternative would create materially ambiguous duplicate representations. Without an official rationale this is not conclusively justified, but the model-cleanup benefit makes the chosen break probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 path would have kept `Contract.term.action.reason` as string plus the R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` siblings, marked them deprecated, and added a separate optional `CodeableReference` element for grouped rationale. That would preserve R4-valid payloads and allow new R6 grouping, but implementations would need rules for conflicts and duplicate same-resource representations; deprecated fields might remain in use indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: That would preserve old instances but duplicate the same rationale facts in one resource, requiring precedence and reconciliation rules that could persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 `Contract.term.action.reason` is `0..*` with type `string` and definition for textual rationale.
evidence.quote: Describes why the action is to be performed or not performed in textual form.

evidence.detail: R4 has `reasonCode` as `0..* CodeableConcept` with example binding to v3 PurposeOfUse.
evidence.quote: Rationale for the action to be performed or not performed.

evidence.detail: R4 has `reasonReference` as `0..* Reference` targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Questionnaire, and QuestionnaireResponse.
R6 `Contract.term.action.reason` is `0..* CodeableReference` with the former reference target set and v3 PurposeOfUse example binding.
evidence.quote: Either a coded concept, or another resource whose existence justifies permitting or not permitting this action.

evidence.detail: R6 `CodeableReference` contains optional `concept` and optional `reference`, each `0..1`.

migrationExampleJson.r4ReasonCode: Map each CodeableConcept to an R6 reason item with concept populated
migrationExampleJson.r4ReasonReference: Map each Reference to an R6 reason item with reference populated

examples.examplesMd: The examples are focused fragments rather than complete valid Contract resources. They illustrate the changed element names and JSON shapes that validators and serializers will encounter.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 consolidates three R4 rationale representations into one `CodeableReference`-based element. This is convenient for new implementations but disruptive for existing data because the old primitive string path is reused with a complex datatype and the two sibling elements disappear. Generated R4 models commonly expose `reason: string[]`, `reasonCode: CodeableConcept[]`, and `reasonReference: Reference[]`; generated R6 models instead expose `reason: CodeableReference[]`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation can fail for two reasons: old `reason` values are primitive strings where R6 expects complex objects, and old `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` are unknown R6 elements. R6-to-R4 conversion requires splitting `CodeableReference` into R4 string/code/reference representations. That split is not always lossless when one R6 item carries both `concept` and `reference`, because R4 has no shared item container to preserve that relationship.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement an explicit transform. Map R4 `reason` strings to R6 `reason.concept.text` unless a project-specific extension is preferred for preserving free text as distinct from coded text. Map each R4 `reasonCode` to an R6 `reason.concept`; map each R4 `reasonReference` to an R6 `reason.reference`. For reverse conversion, flag R6 items containing both `concept` and `reference` for manual review or preserve grouping in an extension. Test all three R4 source fields independently and in combination.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The model cleanup is understandable because `CodeableReference` avoids parallel concept/reference fields. It was not fully backward compatible: a transitional release could have preserved the R4 elements as deprecated aliases or added a new optional element while leaving old paths valid. That alternative would reduce validation breaks but prolong duplicate representations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally includes the removed `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` elements because they are part of the same local remodel and map to the new `CodeableReference` shape.

findings.title: Contract.author can now reference RelatedPerson

oldState.summary: R4 `Contract.author` allowed references to Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.

semanticText.definition: The individual or organization that authored the Contract definition, derivative, or instance in any legal state.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not permit `RelatedPerson` as the author target for the base resource.

newState.summary: R6 adds RelatedPerson to the allowed `Contract.author` reference targets.

semanticText.definition: The individual or organization that authored the Contract definition, derivative, or instance in any legal state.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves all R4 target profiles and adds `RelatedPerson`, making the element broader for new R6 instances.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4-valid `Contract.author` becomes invalid in R6 because this is a widening. The risk appears when R6 data uses `RelatedPerson`; strict R4 validators and generated R4 models constrained to the R4 target set can reject or mishandle that author reference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The author can be legally or operationally important, but use of `RelatedPerson` as the author is likely narrower than practitioner or organization authors.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a related person, such as a family member or representative, to be identified as the source or author of a Contract.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding RelatedPerson widens the R6 target set and preserves all R4-valid author references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of allowing a family member or representative to author a Contract is reasonable, and the base R6 design does not invalidate R4 author references because all R4 targets are retained. The remaining risk is for R6-to-R4 conversion when the new target is used, which is not an R4-to-R6 breaking-design problem.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because this is a target-set widening. Mapping a RelatedPerson author to an R4 extension or rejecting it at an R4 boundary is conversion mitigation, not a backward-compatible base R6 design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoiding the new target would reduce R6-to-R4 down-conversion friction but would exclude a legitimate R6 author type from the base model.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Organization.
R6 preserves the R4 targets and adds RelatedPerson.

migrationExampleJson.r6AuthorRelatedPerson: For R4 output, map to an extension or local profile-specific participant representation, or reject with an explicit conversion error.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows the new target profile; it is not intended as a complete Contract instance.

findings.narrativeMd: `Contract.author` is widened in R6 by adding `RelatedPerson` as an allowed target. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation problem, but it creates a cross-version boundary issue for systems that must down-convert R6 Contract resources to R4 or that generated exhaustive target-type checks from the R4 StructureDefinition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this target set. R6 instances using `author.reference = RelatedPerson/...` are not valid against the R4 base target profiles and require an extension, profile-specific mapping, or rejection when producing R4 output.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 validators, generated reference unions, serializers, and authorization/business rules to accept `RelatedPerson` authors. For R6-to-R4 pipelines, add a deterministic policy for `RelatedPerson` authors rather than silently dropping the author.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because this is a widening, the only strict backward-compatible alternative would be to leave the base R6 target set unchanged and use an extension. That would avoid R6-to-R4 friction but would make a legitimate author type less explicit in the base model.

findings.title: Contract.term.text changed from string to markdown

semanticText.definition: Statement of a provision in a policy or a contract.

oldState.narrativeMd: The element carried a plain string term statement in R4.

semanticText.definition: Statement of a provision in a policy or a contract.

newState.narrativeMd: The JSON value remains a primitive string, but the FHIR type code and expected rendering semantics are now `markdown`.

facts.note: The primitive JSON shape is unchanged even though the FHIR primitive type changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The primitive JSON representation is still a string and R4 already defines the `markdown` primitive as a specialization of string, so ordinary instance payloads are unlikely to fail validation solely because of the value. The practical risk is code generation, schema typing, UI rendering, escaping, and sanitization behavior where `markdown` is treated differently from a plain string.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Term text may be legally meaningful; markdown rendering differences could matter for display, but the underlying text value is preserved.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow formatted contract provision text using the standard FHIR markdown primitive.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Contract.term.text typed as string and clarify in the definition that markdown formatting is allowed or expected.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Formatted contract text is a reasonable R6 goal, and the wire-level compatibility cost is limited because both types serialize as JSON strings. However, the same practical goal could likely have been met by retaining the R4 string type and strengthening the element definition to permit markdown content. The supplied definitions do not show why a computable type change was necessary rather than merely clearer text, so the break in generated models and type metadata is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would leave `Contract.term.text` as `string` and say that the string may contain FHIR markdown. That preserves existing R4-valid values and avoids generated-code churn while still allowing formatted term statements. The tradeoff is weaker machine-readable signaling: validators, UI renderers, and sanitization logic would need to read prose or profile guidance rather than relying on the primitive type code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves R4 payload and generated-type stability, but gives up a computable markdown primitive signal for renderers and sanitizers.

evidence.detail: R6 `markdown` is a primitive type derived from `string`.

term.text: Member may revoke this authorization in writing.
**Member** may revoke this authorization in writing.

examples.examplesMd: The example values remain JSON strings in both versions. The R6 markdown example is representable as an R4 string, but R4 consumers may display markdown syntax literally.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a local type-code change with low instance risk but real implementation risk. Systems that map all FHIR primitives to language strings may see no code change, while systems with distinct generated primitive classes, validation metadata, or UI rendering rules will need to update `Contract.term.text` handling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A normal R4 string value should still satisfy R6 markdown's primitive value shape. R6 markdown text can be sent as an R4 string, but R4 applications may not interpret markdown formatting. Strict generated schemas may report a type-code change even though the JSON scalar shape is unchanged.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and review renderers for markdown sanitization and escaping. Test plain text, markdown syntax, multiline content, and primitive extension cases. Down-conversion to R4 can preserve the string value, but display behavior should be documented.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been avoided by keeping `string` and documenting markdown as allowed content, but the R6 type communicates formatting semantics more clearly and does not usually break raw JSON payloads.

findings.title: Contract.contentDefinition.publicationDate now describes last significant change rather than publication

oldState.summary: R4 defined the date as when the contract was published.

semanticText.definition: The date (and optionally time) when the contract was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the contract changes.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4's first sentence names the element as the publication date, while the rest of the definition already requires updates when version, status, or substantive content changes.

newState.summary: R6 defines the same element as when the contract was last significantly changed.

semanticText.definition: The date (and optionally time) when the contract was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the contract changes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same path, type, cardinality, and short label, but changes the leading semantic from publication time to last significant change time.

facts.newValue: when the contract was last significantly changed

impact.impactRationaleMd: There is no syntactic validation break: the element remains optional `dateTime`. The risk is semantic and business-rule oriented. Systems that stored the original publication date in R4 may produce misleading R6 data if R6 consumers interpret the same value as the last significant change date, while systems using it as an update date may have been aligned with the latter part of the R4 definition already.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Publication and last-change dates can affect contract lifecycle, audit, and legal interpretation. Mislabeling the date could affect business decisions even though validation passes.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that the date tracks meaningful lifecycle changes rather than only initial publication.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve publicationDate as the publication timestamp and add a separate optional last-significant-change element or point to Provenance/relevantHistory.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying lifecycle dates is reasonable, especially because the R4 definition already said the date must change for version, status, and substantive content changes. Still, changing the leading meaning of `publicationDate` in place can make old publication-date data misleading while the path and short label remain unchanged. The same goal could have been met with a clearer additive lifecycle field or history guidance, so this semantic break is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best backward-compatible base design would keep `contentDefinition.publicationDate` focused on the original publication date and add an optional `lastSignificantChangeDate`-style element, or explicitly direct update tracking to `relevantHistory` or Provenance. That preserves R4 semantics for existing values while supporting the R6 lifecycle concept. The cost is a slightly larger model and possible overlap with history metadata.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A new element or explicit history linkage adds model surface area but avoids reinterpreting existing data at the same path.

evidence.detail: R4 says the date is when the contract was published.
evidence.quote: The date (and optionally time) when the contract was published.

evidence.detail: R6 says the date is when the contract was last significantly changed.
evidence.quote: The date (and optionally time) when the contract was last significantly changed.

migrationExampleJson.ifR4ValueMeansOriginalPublication: Preserve the value in an extension or Provenance event and populate R6 publicationDate only if last-significant-change is known.
migrationExampleJson.ifR4ValueAlreadyMeansLastChange: Carry the value forward but document the interpretation.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment remains syntactically valid; it illustrates a value whose business meaning may change.

findings.narrativeMd: The element's wire format is unchanged, but the definition shifts from publication time to last significant change time. That can be breaking for business logic even when validators accept the instance, because the same timestamp may answer a different lifecycle question in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid solely from this text change. The compatibility issue is semantic: R4 data interpreted as original publication date may be wrong for an R6 consumer expecting last significant change, and R6 data interpreted by an R4 consumer may appear to be the original publication date.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit all uses of `contentDefinition.publicationDate`. If the stored value is the original publication date, do not blindly map it to R6 without preserving that meaning, for example via Provenance, `relevantHistory`, or a migration extension. If the value was already maintained as a last-change date, document that policy and add tests around version/status/content updates.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the definition in place is avoidable. A separate last-change element or explicit reliance on Provenance would have preserved backward meaning while adding the new lifecycle concept. The tradeoff is a slightly larger model and possible overlap with history resources.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R4 definition already required the date to change for version, status, or substantive content changes, so some implementations may already treat it as a last-change date. That reduces confidence in real-world impact but does not remove the ambiguity.

findings.title: Contract.term.action performer example bindings changed

oldState.summary: R4 used example bindings to provenance-agent terminology for action performer type and role.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: No authoritative expansions were available for all external value sets.

oldState.narrativeMd: `performerType` was example-bound to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/provenance-agent-type`; `performerRole` was example-bound to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/provenance-agent-role`.

newState.summary: R6 keeps example strength but changes performerType to participation-role-type and performerRole to security-role-type-example.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 local package contains the new value set definitions, but external terminology expansions were not performed.

newState.narrativeMd: The datatype remains `CodeableConcept` and binding strength remains `example`; the suggested terminology sources changed.

facts.newValue: Includes terminology.hl7.org ValueSet/provenance-agent-type and a DICOM value set reference
facts.note: This suggests broadening or repackaging, but expansion was not available locally.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because both bindings remain `example`, base FHIR validation should not reject codes outside the named value sets. The risk is practical rather than hard validation: pick lists, generated examples, terminology recommendations, analytics, and business rules may shift from provenance participant terminology to participation/security role terminology.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect performer role/type suggestions can affect workflow interpretation, but the binding is not normative for validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Align action performer type/role recommendations with broader participation and security-role terminology.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: both performer bindings remain example-strength, so R4 codes are not made invalid by the base R6 resource.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local definitions show a recommendation shift from provenance participant terminology to participation and security-role examples, but they do not provide the rationale or full terminology expansions. Because the bindings remain `example`, this does not create an R4-to-R6 validation break in the base resource. The practical impact is on pick lists, analytics, and local profiles, so the necessity of the terminology change cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for preserving R4 instances because example bindings do not constrain base validation. Publishing ConceptMaps, listing old value sets as additional guidance, or documenting migration from the R4 examples would be useful mitigation for implementers, but those are terminology guidance measures rather than alternatives to avoid a base R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining old value sets as additional guidance could ease migration, but that is terminology transition support rather than a less-breaking base design needed to preserve R4 instances.

evidence.detail: The R6 local participation-role-type ValueSet composes in `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/provenance-agent-type` and a DICOM value set reference.

examples.examplesMd: No concrete invalid instance example is provided because example bindings do not make non-member codes invalid in the base resource.

findings.narrativeMd: The performer elements retain the same datatype and cardinality, but their example terminology recommendations changed. This matters for implementations that treated example bindings as UI pick lists, local enums, or analytics categories even though base FHIR validation treats them as non-binding examples.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no hard validation break from the base binding strength. Compatibility risk appears in generated terminology helpers, seeded pick lists, documentation-driven workflows, and any local profiles that strengthened these example bindings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review UI lists and local profile bindings for `performerType` and `performerRole`. If R4 value sets were used operationally, compare them with the R6 recommended value sets using an authoritative terminology server and add ConceptMap or local mapping guidance where needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could be made easier to consume by publishing explicit terminology mappings or retaining old value sets as additional guidance. Because the base binding is only example, a hard backward-compatible model alternative is less important than migration documentation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology impact is limited by example binding strength, but local profiles may have strengthened these bindings and should be checked separately.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R6 retains the same canonical URL, id, type, resource kind, `DomainResource` baseDefinition, specialization derivation, and non-abstract flag. The status changed from draft to active but not in a way that changes instance shape.

No common local Contract element had a min or max cardinality change. The two removed R4 reason sibling elements are covered by the action-reason remodel finding rather than counted as cardinality changes.

No local Contract-specific invariants were added, removed, or strengthened. Snapshot differences in `dom-*`, `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and missing `xpath` are inherited/base-artifact concerns and were excluded.
No local Contract element changed modifier status. Differences seen on inherited `implicitRules` wording or base `modifierExtension` handling are out of scope for this resource report.
No local Contract summary flag change with material impact was found. The visible root `modifierExtension` summary-flag change is inherited from the base resource model and excluded.
No local Contract slicing changes were found in the compared snapshots.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value changes were found.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value-limit changes were found for Contract elements.

Required bindings for `Contract.status` and `Contract.contentDefinition.publicationStatus` still point to the same canonical value sets and local CodeSystems with the same 15 status codes. Several example/extensible bindings rely on external terminology not fully available in the local R6 core package; material performer-binding changes are reported separately.

No reference target narrowing was found. The only local target-set widening identified is `Contract.author` adding `RelatedPerson`, reported separately. The action-reason reference targets moved into `CodeableReference` and are covered by the remodel finding.

No resource-level serialization identity change was found. Serialization impact is localized to `term.action.reason` changing from primitive/string and sibling fields to `CodeableReference`, and to codegen-level primitive typing for `term.text`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The resource identity, canonical URL, type, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are unchanged. The status metadata change does not alter instance validation shape by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance or documentation workflows that filter by artifact status may treat the R6 Contract definition differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Contract status binding version changed but local status codes were unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both R4 and R6 bind `Contract.status` with required strength to the same canonical value set and local CodeSystem containing the same 15 status codes. The R6 short text uses `executable +`, but the computable CodeSystem did not remove the other status codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators should not infer code removal from the shortened display text alone; use the CodeSystem/ValueSet definitions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publication status binding version changed but local status codes were unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The required binding remains on the same canonical value set, and the local R4/R6 `contract-publicationstatus` CodeSystems both contain the same 15 codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not treat the R6 `amended ... executable +` short text as a computable restriction without checking the CodeSystem.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records `mustSupport: false` on many elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omitted `mustSupport` on many base elements, which is equivalent to false. R6's explicit false values do not create a support obligation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Diff tooling should normalize omitted `mustSupport` and explicit `false` to avoid false-positive changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Security label explanatory text was clarified
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element path, cardinality, datatype, flags, and bindings were not materially changed. The R6 text appears to move and tighten explanatory material about term and nested term security labels.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Security-label policy engines should still be checked against local profiles, but the base resource comparison did not show a computable constraint change here.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The main Contract breaking change depends on the R6 `CodeableReference` datatype. A datatype-level report should assess its own R4/R6 compatibility and conversion patterns.
Inherited snapshot differences were intentionally excluded from this Contract report, including base constraints, `language`, `modifierExtension`, and extension constraint differences.
The performer binding finding is limited by absent authoritative expansions and ConceptMaps. Terminology-specific review should compare expansions and intended mappings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, Jira ticket, or change note was supplied. Justification and backward-compatible-alternative assessments are therefore inferred from the computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official ballot change logs, Jira issues, or specification diff pages for Contract.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Local package terminology resources were compared where present, but no terminology server expansion was run. Some R6 bindings reference external terminology resources not included in the local R6 core package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Expand the affected R4 and R6 value sets with the same terminology server and compare code membership, inactive codes, and designations.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages and examples were not compared. Semantic findings rely on StructureDefinition element text only.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare the R4 and R6 Contract narrative pages, examples, and implementation notes.
